answer: Randomness-gated identity renewal. Each identity must periodically solve a challenge seeded by a public verifiable random beacon, so the work cannot be precomputed or batched in advance. Only solvers that wander through the full search space earn the nectar of continued standing. Because the seed is unknown until published, an attacker running many identities must pay fresh compute per identity per epoch, and duplicate vines collapse onto the same unpredictable seed, forcing parallel expenditure rather than shared preparation.
